question: Using Section 8B.03 and Figure 8B-2, describe the vertical order of a passive-crossing assembly with multiple tracks and a YIELD or STOP sign, and state when the Number of Tracks plaque is required.
model_answer: Direct Answer: At a passive grade crossing with two or more tracks, the assembly reads from top to bottom: the Crossbuck (R15-1) sign at the top of the support, the inverted-T Number of Tracks (R15-2P) plaque mounted directly below the Crossbuck, and the YIELD (R1-2) or STOP (R1-1) sign mounted below the plaque on the same support (as shown in Figure 8B-2). The Number of Tracks plaque is required whenever two or more tracks are present at the crossing. Standards (mandatory): - "A Crossbuck Assembly shall consist of a Crossbuck (R15-1) sign, and a Number of Tracks (R15-2P) plaque if two or more tracks are present, that complies with the provisions of Section 8B.03, and either a YIELD (R1-2) or STOP (R1-1) sign installed on the same support, except as provided in Paragraph 10 of this Section. YIELD or STOP signs used at passive grade crossings shall be installed in compliance with the provisions of Section 2B.18, and Figures 8B-2 and 8B-3." - "If there are two or more tracks at a grade crossing, the number of tracks shall be indicated on a supplemental Number of Tracks (R15-2P) plaque (see Figure 8B-1) of inverted T shape mounted below the Crossbuck sign in the manner shown in Figure 8B-2." - "If a Crossbuck sign support at a passive grade crossing does not include a YIELD or STOP sign..., a vertical strip of retroreflective white material, not less than 2 inches in width, shall be used for the full length of the front of the support from the Crossbuck sign or Number of Tracks plaque to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway." Guidance (recommended): - The use of STOP signs at passive grade crossings should be limited to unusual conditions where requiring all motor vehicles to make a full stop is determined necessary by a Diagnostic Team; figure notes reiterate that YIELD or STOP signs are used only at passive crossings, with STOP used only if an engineering study determines it appropriate, and mounting heights of at least 4 feet on existing Crossbuck supports and at least 5 feet (rural) or 7 feet (parking/pedestrian areas) for new installations. - If the YIELD or STOP sign is on a separate support, it should be in the same plane as the Crossbuck sign, closer to the traveled way, with a minimum 2-inch separation between the nearest points of the two signs. Options (permitted): - A strip of retroreflective white material not less than 2 inches in width may be used on the back of each blade of each Crossbuck sign at active grade crossings. Visual evidence: [Image 1] Figure 8E-5 shows the vertical stacking at a pathway/sidewalk crossing — RAILROAD CROSSING Crossbuck at top, "2 TRACKS" plaque below it, then a YIELD or STOP sign below the plaque on the same support. [Image 2] Figure 8B-1 depicts the individual sign designs, including the R15-1 Crossbuck and the inverted-T R15-2P "3 TRACKS" plaque. [Image 3] shows the full Section 8E.05 page with the same top-to-bottom assembly arrangement. [Image 4] shows Figure 8B-2, the definitive illustration of the highway Crossbuck Assembly: Crossbuck at top (approximately 9 ft mounting height), "3 TRACKS" plaque below, and YIELD or STOP sign below the plaque, with mounting-height notes. [Image 5] shows the Section 8B.04 text page containing the mounting-height and retroreflective-strip Standards. [Image 6] shows Table 8B-1 (Sheet 2) and the Section 8B.04 Standard requiring the Crossbuck, Number of Tracks plaque (if two or more tracks), and YIELD or STOP sign on the same support. Citations: - Section 8B.04 Standard §1 (p.995) - Section 8B.03 Standard §6 (p.993) - Section 8B.04 Standard §20 (p.1000) - Section 8B.04 Guidance §6 (p.997) - Section 8B.04 Guidance §13 (p.1000) - Section 8B.03 Option §9 (p.995) - Figure 8E-5 (p.1039) - Figure 8B-1 (p.996) - Page 1041 - Page 1080 - Page 1038 - Page 1036
gold_answer: The Crossbuck is at the top, the inverted-T Number of Tracks plaque is directly below it, and the YIELD or STOP sign is below the plaque on the support. The Number of Tracks plaque is required when two or more tracks are present.
